doc.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Favorite sidemen on dates
summary: He names tenor players King Curtis, Sam Taylor, David Newman and guitarists Mickey Baker, Eric Gale and others, and contrasts rhythm sections with horn players who play what is on the page.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who were the people in the key positions, the bass player, the guitar and even like the tenor sax soloists that you liked to see on the date?
King Curtis was the tenor sax soloist. Sam “the Man” Taylor, David Newman, Marshall Royal. I mean all these guys were all legends to me. And guitar players was Mickey

Baker, Eric Gale, Hugh McCracken, David Spinozza, Vinnie Bell, Wally Richardson. I mean these guitar — and Bucky Pizzarelli. I mean for me I could not have ever asked for anybody any better than those musicians. I mean there were hundreds that you could go along with the program with and have them on the date and it would automatically turn out. But you had to know who you put together. It was the people that you put together that liked one another that made things happen even when the music was wrong they wouldn’t play it wrong. They just wanted to be — yeah, not in the rhythm section. Horns? Ahh see the horn section and the string section, until that arranger would want to change it or correct it, they’d just go and play it.
They wouldn’t say anything if it sounded off.
No. And that’s what I used to come down on see. That was the thing that I was hollering across the room, oy yoy yoy.
Okay so he might have been playing what was on the page.
But it wasn’t what should have been there.
And I would tell them, “You know you’re playing the wrong note, why don’t you just change it?” And I was good at that. I was hollering all across the place. I was always hollering across the place.
